comment.body:
I asked Claude AI to evaluate a section from my upcoming (really, someday! 😆) book, a section where I explain how coercive authority is irrational, as in crazy.

 

Of course, it began with the customary misreads and fallacious objections. I pretty much know them all at this point.

 

Once I pointed out its mistakes, all of its criticisms and objections were taken off the table. It ended up agreeing completely.

 

I'm ready to say that coercive authority is a manifestation of mental illness.

 

Coming soon. (really)

 

(Here's the link if you want to read the convo and get a peek at a bit of the book: https://claude.ai/share/977fe47f-1551-41c7-aa15-7780bb0be717 )

comment.body:
Just a little recalibration of what has come to be considered normal when it's anything but…

I'm pretty sure that hunter-gatherers didn't liken their lives to a “rat race”. 

PS. Just as an example of how insidious it all is, they weren't hunter-gatherers. They were gatherer-hunters. The mind-conditioning is built right into our language.

linkMetadata.title: Farmers have less leisure time than hunter-gatherers, study suggests
linkMetadata.description: Hunter-gatherers in the Philippines who convert to farming work around ten hours a week longer than their forager neighbours, a new study suggests, complicating the idea that agriculture represents progress. The research also shows that the adoption of agriculture impacts most on the lives of women.

comment.body:
//

It's not going to start in London. The change will start in the East. It's Eastern Europe that's going to snap first, because they've been pushed to the fucking edge. Not with Netflix and Starbucks. Not with rainbow flags and safe zones and distractions... With poverty with militarization with foreign puppets running the damn show.

They said EU will bring prosperity. Where is it? Half the youth is gone working in kitchens abroad. The governments don't protect them. They sell them. They sell them to Brussels, to NATO, and to whoever pays better.

These people, my people, they remember what dictatorship feels like. They remember the propaganda. They remember the checkpoints, the lies dressed as law. They’ve seen this cycle before, and they are done pretending this is freedom. And when they rise—when they rise—they won't be asking for reforms. They'll be demanding for heads. They'll be shaking the system.

Because when obedience becomes death, rebellion is survival.

//
